To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have constructed two linear bases of the centralizer algebra of $Pin(N)(\Delta\bigotimes \textstyle{\otimes^kV})$ which are parametrized by the'spinor Brauer diagrams' and we have given the multiplication formulas for these two bases.
we find the irreducible spinor representations in $\Delta \otimes \bigoplus_k V^{\otimes k}$.
we have found a new kind of linear basis in the centralizer algebra for the spinor group and we can use this basis to construct the irreducible spin representation in the tensor space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the representation theory for the spinor group, which is a natural generalization of the classical Brauer theory for orthogonal groups.
the centralizer algebra for the spinor group and the irreducible spin representation.
the representation theory and invariant theory of the Spinor groups and their applications in the theory of the Brauer algebras and the Schur-Wyman reciprocity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spinor groups are the natural generalization of the orthogonal group, the spin representations are the natural generalizations of the vector representations and the Schur-Way reciprocity is the natural generalization for the centralizer algebra of the orthogonal group.

the centralizer algebra for $Pin(N) \times \frak{S}$ in $\Delta \otimes \bigoplus^k V$ is the same as the centralizer algebra of $\frak{A}$ in $\bigoplus^l \Delta$ for $Pin(l)$, where $\frak{a}$ is the fundamental representation for $Spin(l)$ and $l=2k$.
we have established a spinor version of Schur-Weyr reciprocity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we give a new construction for the irreducible spinor representations of $Spin(N)$ and give the transformation matrices for them.
the irreducible spin representation $\Delta \textstile{\otimes} \textstile{k} \Delta$ is a 'dual' to the Brauer centralizer $\mathbf{B}_k$, which is a 'duality' of the Schur- Weyl reciprocity.
we establish an isomorphism between the centralizer algebra and the algebra of the symmetric group invariants in $\Delta \otimes \bigoplus^k V$ and give the explicit transformation matrices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are able to construct the spin representations of the spinor groups by using the centralizer algebra of $Pin(N)$.
, the spinor groups have more interesting representation theory than their orthogonal counterparts.
